hypothesis: For the monomial z_n = x^(2^n) over Mul = {x, ×} and Sq = {x, ×, sq} with sq(y)=y·y definable, the four seams separate exactly: (US-1) both languages realise every positive degree; (US-2) every Mul-tree of degree 2^n has size 2^{n+1}-1 while a Sq-tower has size n+1; (US-3) sharing-circuit size is n in both bases; (US-4) under the Gibbs prior π(t)∝4^{-|t|}, language-normalised fiber mass satisfies log2(P_Sq/P_Mul) ≥ 2·(2^{n+1}-n-2)+log2(Z_Mul/Z_Sq)-log2(C_{2^n-1}), and at n=4 the Sq fiber occupies 27 size shells against one Catalan shell of 9694845 Mul-trees.
target_object: The monomial x^(2^n) as a denotation class (degree) in two expression languages.
decision: Accept the four-seam separation on this toy if and only if all six noncompensatory gates pass. Do not promote US-4′ (EML gradient recovery).
representation_and_data_clock: Finite expression trees and sharing DAGs. Degree is the denotation. No sampling clock; exact integer DP plus closed-form partition functions.
material_assumptions: Denotation is monomial degree; × adds degrees and sq doubles degree.
Tree size is node count; circuit size is the number of mul/sq steps after the leaf x.
Gibbs prior is π(t) ∝ 4^{-|t|} with language-level partition functions Z_Mul=2-√3 and Z_Sq=(3-√5)/2.
sq is a definable macro, so the extension is conservative on denotations.

gates.SS_EXPRESSIVITY_CONSERVATIVE_EXTENSION: Every degree in 1..16 is realised by at least one Mul-tree and one Sq-tree.
gates.SS_TREE_SIZE_EXACT: For each n in {1,2,3,4}, Mul size is 2^{n+1}-1 and the Sq-tower size is n+1.
gates.SS_CATALAN_SINGLE_SHELL: The Mul fiber of degree 2^n is exactly C_{2^n-1} trees on a single size shell.
gates.SS_CIRCUIT_SIZE_THETA_N: Repeated squaring reaches degree 2^n in n steps, and max degree after k steps is ≤ 2^k on the tower and two alternative circuits.
gates.SS_FIBER_MASS_EXCEEDS_SHORTEST_BOUND: For every registered n, log2(P_Sq/P_Mul) is at least the amended shortest-witness bound; at n=4 the ratio is at least 28.28.
gates.SS_SHELL_OCCUPANCY: The Sq fiber occupies every size from n+1 through 2^{n+1}-1 (27 shells at n=4).

amendment_after_run_1.reason: Run 1 used unnormalised Φ as if it were discovery probability. The Gibbs probability is Φ/Z.

compute.sampling: none; exact integer DP and closed-form generating functions.

mathematical_claim_card.objects: MulTree, SqTree, degree : Tree → ℕ≥1, size : Tree → ℕ≥1, CircStep DAGs, Catalan numbers, Gibbs masses Φ,Z.
mathematical_claim_card.types_domains_units: Degree is a dimensionless exponent. Size is node count. Circuit size is step count. Masses are dimensionless probabilities after /Z.
mathematical_claim_card.claim_and_quantifiers: ∀ n ∈ ℕ, every Mul-tree of degree 2^n has size 2^{n+1}-1; ∃ Sq-tree of degree 2^n and size n+1; ∀ sharing circuits, max degree after k steps ≤ 2^k, hence ≥ n steps are necessary for degree 2^n; for n∈{1,2,3,4} the Gibbs ratio meets the shortest-witness bound.
mathematical_claim_card.assumptions: No cancellation in the multiplicative monoid; sq is definable as y×y; Gibbs base 4 is a modelling choice, not a derived constant.
mathematical_claim_card.derivation_dependencies: Structural induction on trees; Catalan enumeration of full binary trees; generating-function solutions of A=x+xA^2 and A=x+xA+xA^2.
mathematical_claim_card.invariance: Degree is basis-invariant. Tree size is not. Circuit size is sharing-invariant across the two bases.
mathematical_claim_card.edge_cases: n=0 is the leaf x (size 1 both sides). Even sizes appear only after sq is added.
mathematical_claim_card.executable_checks: DP counts match Catalan; closed-form Z evaluated at 1/4; n=4 headline 7.8e-12 vs 4.0e-3.
